title: CtlCreateRequest
description: `POST /v1/tenants`: the mutation envelope of `op_request.json` with TYPED `args`. Everything that decides what code runs is an ID into something a trusted operator prepared on the CLI: `artifact_id` (never a git ref or path), images from `settings.images`, the Python env from the artifact. `settings` accepts PUBLIC keys only, with the same name guard as the registry — `template_from` copies the named tenant's public settings and nothing else. Keys are described by `{label, role}`; their VALUES are minted server-side and delivered once through `GET /v1/jobs/{id}/secrets`. `admin_subjects` are `issuer:sub` with issuer = `identity_provider`, refused when the provider is `none`.

PublicSettingKey.description: Byte-identical to `registry.json#/$defs/PublicSettingKey` (pattern, anyOf and all) — asserted by `conformance/ctl/test_contract_static.py`. The forbidden pattern is `go/internal/ctl/settings/settings.go`'s `secretPattern` and the `anyOf` enum its `publicDespitePattern`.

es_heap.description: JVM heap for the dedicated Elasticsearch, e.g. `1g`. Admission checks the fleet heap sum against host memory.

postgres.description: Where the tenant keeps its ACL, job and collection state. `sqlite` (the default) is files under `<data_dir>/state` and runs no server. `local` gives the tenant its OWN postgres instance on the block's +5 port, supervised by a `ragstack-<name>-postgres.service` the ctl owns: it adds `TENANT_PG_PASSWORD` and the three `*_DSN` lines to `secrets.env`, and a `postgres` leg to `start`/`stop`/`restart --only`. `external` — a database inside a server somebody else runs — is NOT offered here: it needs an admin DSN, which is a CLI-only, trusted-operator input.

keys.description: Keys to mint. At least one `admin` key is always minted (the bootstrap admin the ctl itself uses to register service accounts), whether or not it is listed here.

template_from.description: Copy this tenant's PUBLIC settings as a starting point.

supervisor.description:
How the ctl starts and stops the new tenant. `systemd`: `ragstack-<name>.target` under the account's user manager — rendered units, linked and enabled. `instance`: the ctl supervises it itself (an `apptainer instance` per exclusively-owned store, a detached uvicorn with a pidfile for the api, `@reboot` in the account's crontab for boot) and writes NO unit files. `manual` is not offered: it describes a tenant somebody else started, which is what `adopt` records, not something `create` can produce.

The DEFAULT the ctl applies comes from `ctl.env`'s `CTL_DEFAULT_SUPERVISOR` (on coconut, `instance`). The schema default below is what the CONTRACT promises when the deployment says nothing, and the two are deliberately allowed to differ: which supervisor a host can actually run is a fact about that host, not about the API.

gateway.description: Publish a gateway generation that routes the new tenant.
